extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers applying for NIH K99/R00 awards and their mentors (and NIH reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Review criteria and sample reviewer critiques for an NIH NIA K99/R00 Pathway to Independence application, showing how reviewers score Candidate, Career Development, Research Plan, Mentors, Environment, human subjects protections, inclusion, and other reviewable elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the applicant's qualifications, prior research experience, productivity, and potential to become an independent investigator (e.g., publication record, prior funding, relevant training).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note strengths (e.g., relevant training in sociology, publications, prior pilot funding, commitment to the area) and weaknesses (e.g., limited research experience or insufficient first-author PubMed-indexed publications). Scored numerically by reviewers (example scores shown: 1–3 across critiques).

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Plan/Career Goals/Plan to Provide Mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality, relevance, and feasibility of the proposed career development and mentoring plan, including training activities, experiential learning, professional development (grant writing, publications), and mentoring structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good plans have clearly laid out objectives, appropriate coursework/experiences, and targeted experiential training (e.g., clinical shadowing, implementation science training). Weaknesses include components that are not directly relevant or are standard/common training, and insufficient plans to increase manuscript productivity. Reviewers scored this element separately (example scores shown: 2–4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific rationale, significance, coherence of aims, methodological rigor, feasibility, sample size justification, and appropriateness of proposed measures and analyses for the proposed research (including dependency among aims and potential heterogeneity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths include well-developed aims that build logically and potential high impact. Common weaknesses noted: over-reliance of later aims on success of Aim 1 without adequate justification or preliminary data; sample sizes based on convenience; underpowered design for some hypotheses; lack of justification for specific measures (e.g., goal-attainment scaling) or plans to handle heterogeneity (different dementia types, clinician types). Reviewers recommend clearer justification of feasibility, recruitment plans, power, and contingency plans if Aim 1 yields unexpected findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor(s), Co-Mentor(s), Consultant(s), Collaborator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifications, track records, complementary expertise, mentoring history, and appropriateness of the proposed mentoring/advisory team for training the candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths: established, interdisciplinary mentors with relevant expertise and mentoring records. Suggested improvements: adding clinicians with focused dementia practice (e.g., behavioral neurologist) if absent. Reviewers consider presence of necessary expertise and history of mentoring K awardees as positives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment and Institutional Commitment to the Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional resources, research environment, facilities, access to patient populations/partnerships, and explicit institutional commitment to the candidate's career development (including potential R00 recruitment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths include outstanding environment, specific cores/resources (e.g., Clinical Research Methodology Core), and institutional letters showing commitment. Weaknesses rarely noted but absence of commitment would be a concern. This criterion is scored separately (example scores: 1–2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequacy of plans to protect human subjects: risks, confidentiality, informed consent, reporting adverse events, data security, and procedures for emergent issues (abuse, suicidality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer statement: 'Acceptable Risks and Adequate Protections.' Documented protections include IRB oversight, secure storage of paper and electronic data, coding of participant IDs, limits to confidentiality disclosed in consent, and procedures to contact social worker/psychiatrist if abuse or suicidality detected. Reviewers evaluate whether protections are adequate and note any concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans and justification for inclusion/exclusion by sex/gender, race/ethnicity, and age (including exclusion of children when appropriate); recruitment targets and rationale (e.g., oversampling groups of interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers found plans 'Acceptable' when distributions are justified scientifically. Examples: targeting equal numbers of African-American and white caregivers, expected gender distributions based on workforce and caregiver demographics, excluding those under 18 with justification. For NIH-defined Phase III trials, valid design and analysis plans are required. Reviewers note when inclusion plans lack detail for specific trial phases or outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Planned RCR training activities and whether they satisfy NIH requirements for ethical conduct of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In examples, reviewers marked 'Acceptable.' Guidance: training should satisfy the requirement and be clearly described (coursework, mentoring, instruction). Reviewers will flag inadequate detail or absence of a plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans to monitor data integrity and participant safety across the study, including accounting for institutional changes and procedures for oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers considered the plan 'Acceptable' when it accounted for potential institutional change and provided appropriate monitoring mechanisms. For clinical trials, reviewers expect monitoring commensurate with risk and trial phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for sharing data, tools, and other resources produced by the project (e.g., dissemination and sharing of a developed toolkit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked 'Acceptable' when plans exist for data sharing; reviewers noted when dissemination details are lacking (example: plan did not detail how the toolkit will be disseminated/shared). Applicants should describe specific dissemination and sharing mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support / Committee Budget Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the requested budget and recommended adjustments; whether budget is reasonable and period of support is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee recommended the budget 'Recommend as Requested' in the sample. Administrative note: the budget shown is the requested budget and may be recalculated by grants management staff based on committee recommendations. Reviewers evaluate appropriateness of costs and may recommend adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (Impact Score) and Scoring Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall impact score reflects reviewers' assessment of the likelihood that the candidate will be successful; the impact/priority score is calculated after discussion by averaging overall scores (1–9) from voting reviewers and multiplying by 10. Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting and are not specifically discussed or mathematically combined into the overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance from NIH: criterion scores (e.g., Candidate, Career Development, Research Plan, Mentors, Environment) are provided by assigned reviewers before the meeting; the overall impact score is determined after discussion. Percentiles may be provided for some applications. Applicants should understand scoring mechanics and that written critiques may be prepared prior to the meeting and not revised after group discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments on Format, Subject Matter, Faculty Participation, Duration, Frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative/commentary categories reviewers may use to note concerns or acceptability about the application's formatting, topical appropriateness, faculty participation, duration, and frequency of proposed activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the sample these were noted as 'No concern' or 'Acceptable.' Reviewers will flag problems in formatting or inappropriate scope/schedule. Ensure application follows funding opportunity instructions and format requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment and certification regarding use of live vertebrate animals in the application (presence/absence and compliance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the sample: 'No live vertebrate animals involved for competing appl.' Reviewers check whether animal use is proposed and whether appropriate protections and justifications are provided when applicable.
